brief: Goldman's Brian Garrett (FICC & Equities) opens a week-prep note on 2 Oct with positioning context: with one quarter left in 2026, net exposure to US equities sits at 1-, 3- and 5-year lows, and the spread in exposure across regions is extreme, with funds max long Asia and Europe. He frames "not bullish America" as a crowded trade, and argues that because a move to SPX 8100 would hurt funds positioned this way, upside is not expensive. He admits his own view falls within that consensus (tight net exposure, given rates, oil, geopolitics, credit, bonds) but flags the view itself is extremely consensus, i.e. a crowding risk, not a forecast. Attached is Erin Tolar's Prime Brokerage "First Look" on September hedge fund data: Global Fundamental L/S funds returned -0.55%, outperforming the benchmark; equities were modestly net sold as short sales outpaced long buys, and gross trading activity rose at its fastest pace in four months; gross leverage rose while net leverage fell; net selling in EM Asia and North America was mostly offset by buying in Europe; and funds rotated into TMT while nearly every other sector was net sold.
